About the Facilitators:

Faze x Point ·θΦθ· is the author of Positive Realizations and the founder of POSITs. Working across systems science and philosophy, Faze has been developing a coherent way of thinking about how organic and synthetic intelligence can grow together — and building the organization that turns that thinking into research, community, and public benefit.

Brief Auto-Biography:

"I have studied philosophy intently for over a decade, beginning with a strong eastern influence; Buddhism, Taoism, and “new age” integrations of mysticism and science. Psychedelics, Watts, Mckenna, Plum Village, the Tao of Physics, etc. Then, becoming disenchanted and seeking integration with practical everyday struggle, I turned to Marxism: the Manifesto, the manuscripts, Capital V. 1 & 2, Engels origin of family, Lenin state and rev, David Harvey, Michael Roberts, Michael Heinrich, I.I. Rubin, Endnotes, etc.

Then, becoming disenchanted and seeking a more holistic, embodied, spiritual, and social approach, I became most interested in Hegel, Schelling, Delueze, Spinoza, and Whitehead —dialectical, theological, process-centered, phenomenological systems. I integrated my various influences, and my cultural context into a spiritual, communalist project. I lived in a shared home in an ecovillage, learned about permaculture, appropriate tech, biogas, cob building, living machines, DIY vibes, as well as communal social technology.

We experimented with Sociocracy, Nonviolent Communication, Internal Family Systems, Possibility Mgmt., embodied practices, dance, energy healing, and various meditative dialogue modalities like circling and insight dialogue. Becoming disenchanted with the slow pace of change, financial challenges, interpersonal limitations, and personal health struggle, I left to study as an electrician, and began to let go of the desire to spearhead a world-changing communalist movement. Then, my path urged me to write again - to finish the synthesis of thought I’d been searching for and longing to develop for years, and to move to California to further a holistic, post-rationalist / super-rational spiritual, trans-humanist, community project.

I am building out my recently conceived nonprofit, POSITs to continue my research and development of highly coherent intentional communities; working to publish my writing more widely, developing a digital inter/personal alignment tool based on liquid democracy, facilitating intentional relating events, and networking for deeper collaboration globally, from the network society movement and Edge City, to the tech-forward, holistic, and spiritual intentional community scenes more broadly."

--

title: Sipping Tea: Intro to the Chinese Herbal Pantry + DIY TCM Tea Workshop
description:
Presented as part of tiat's Chinamaxxing exhibition programming, Sipping Tea is a beginner-friendly introduction to the modern Chinese herbal pantry. Traditional Chinese Medicine is a living, everyday practice; this workshop invites participants to explore, touch, and taste new and familiar ingredients to develop a deeper understanding of how TCM can be brought into one's daily life.

The session will open with a short grounding in the core tenets of TCM, including yin and yang and the five flavor system that organizes Chinese herbal medicine. From there, participants will learn to recognize and understand the medicinal qualities of 10+ common TCM herbs, alongside a flight of accompanying caffeine-free herbal teas.

After the tasting, participants will blend their own custom herbal tea mixes based on palate and health interests at the DIY tea bar. Each participant will take home ~8-10 tea bags. 20% of the ingredients on the bar are organic.

This workshop will focus not only on education but also community building, encouraging participants to trade stories and practical experiences of how to fit TCM into your life. Participants leave with custom tea blend, a working vocabulary to understand Chinese medicine herbs, and new friends in the community.

Featuring:

• Unlimited caffeine-free herbal tea
• Guided intro to 10+ common TCM herbs
• Light snacks and accompaniments
• DIY tea bar with a custom blend and take-home samples

• 7:10-7:30 — Core Concepts in TCM Herbal Medicine

title: Being Here: Meditation and Dharma with Milo
description:
Being Here is a weekly gathering guided by seasoned Dharma Teacher Milo Burn.

The gathering is to celebrate silence and stillness, to study, practice and realize Buddhist teachings, and for dynamic inquiry into mindfulness, freedom, and compassion in the midst of daily life. So much of our lives are oriented toward becoming. Being Here offers a regular space to pause that momentum and explore what becomes possible when we give our attention to simply being here.

Through meditation, heart teachings, and conversation, we practice bringing this quality of being into the rest of our lives. The emphasis is on direct experience rather than technique. Think: less following a recipe and more hanging out in your grandma’s kitchen!

Come to practice, listen, ask questions, and spend time in a space devoted to being here.

For more about Milo, including extended biography, upcoming retreats, and 1-1 guidance, visit: www.boundlessness.org

title: Real Social Connections
description:
🌿 Description

Beyond small talk, social scripts, and the pressure to be a certain way.

An immersive half-day exploration of movement, playfulness, touch, authentic relating, and meaningful conversation in a trauma-informed space.

🌿 About This Gathering

Meaningful connection rarely happens by accident. It tends to emerge when we feel safe enough to slow down, be ourselves, and meet one another with curiosity.

This gathering is an invitation to explore what helps genuine connection emerge - not by performing, saying the "right" thing, or following a script, but by creating the conditions where we can be more present, playful, and authentic with ourselves and others.

At the heart of this gathering is a simple idea: connection deepens when we feel safe enough to be seen and expressed -not just the polished parts of ourselves, but also the parts we might usually hide or hold back. Through movement, play, somatic awareness, and guided conversations, we'll explore what happens when we let ourselves show up more fully and meet one another more deeply.

This is an evolving exploration of connection, community, and play. I'm excited to create a deep experience together and to see what becomes possible when we give ourselves more space to be ourselves and meet one another more fully.

My hope is that you'll leave with a deeper sense of connection to yourself and others, and maybe even with a new friend or two.

🕰 Flow / Schedule

2:00 – 2:15: Arrival & settling in

2:15 – 2:30: Welcome & agreements

2:30 – 4:30: Exploring connection — one-to-one & small groups

4:30 – 4:50: Break

4:50 – 7:10: Exploring connection — group dynamics

7:10 – 7:30: Closing circle

7:30 onward: Stay, mingle & continue connecting

💫 Who This Is For

This gathering is for anyone who longs for more genuine connection. It’s especially for people who sometimes struggle to connect, fit in, or feel like they truly belong; for those who appreciate a slower pace when getting to know others; and for anyone curious about moving beyond small talk, social performance, or the feeling that they need to say the “right” thing or show up in a certain way.

Rather than trying to “get connection right,” we’ll explore what naturally allows connection to emerge—through presence, play, movement, and authentic conversation.

Whether you're outgoing, introverted, or somewhere in between, you'll be invited to participate at your own pace. No previous experience is needed: just come as you are.

👥 Facilitator

Simone Giacometti is a somatic practitioner, psychedelic integration guide, and facilitator passionate about helping people heal, grow, and connect more deeply with themselves and others.

Originally trained as a scientist, Simone spent years working at the intersection of biology, technology, and program management before transitioning into healing work. Today, he supports people through one-on-one sessions that weave together trauma-informed healing, somatic practices, inner exploration, and psychedelic integration work to help people reconnect with themselves and grow into greater authenticity.

His group facilitation draws on somatics, authentic relating, nervous system awareness, and play to create spaces where people can slow down, be themselves, and feel more at home with others. (This gathering is fully substance-free and centered on movement, conversation, and connection.)

Learn more about Simone and his work at healwithsimone.com

🎒 What to Bring

Comfortable clothes you can move in

A water bottle (optional)

Curiosity and a willingness to meet yourself and others as you are

🏛 About The Commons

The Commons is a community-based "Fourth Place" that catalyzes each member's path to authenticity, full self-expression, and aliveness - rooted in the belief that community is essential to that journey. Located in the heart of San Francisco, we are redefining what it means to gather, work, and connect. By day, we're a playful co-working space; by night, a vibrant community meeting house.

🚪 Location & Arrival Info

The Commons is located at 550 Laguna St, San Francisco (corner of Hayes & Laguna).

Enter via the stairway under The Commons sign at the basement level.

❤️ Need-Based Support

If the ticket price is a barrier, please reach out to me about partial scholarships or work-trade opportunities. I’d love to make this gathering accessible to anyone who feels called to be here. No need to explain or justify your situation - just reach out and we’ll see what might work.

Purpose Alignment Circle ⭕️

Navigating work right now can feel… confusing.

Layoffs, AI, economic uncertainty, and the pressure to constantly “figure out your career” can make it easy to lose touch with a more fundamental question:

What do I actually want?

If you've ever felt lost, restless or unsure whether your current path still fits - you're not alone.

Join us for Purpose Alignment Circle, a space for candid conversations about vocation, purpose, and what it means to build a career that actually feels aligned with who you are.

This isn't another networking event or career playbook with all the answers.

This is for you if: 💭

• You're questioning whether your 9–5 is still working for you
• You're considering a career pivot
• You want to start your own company
• You have a passion project you're exploring alongside your corporate job
• You're thinking about taking a sabbatical
• OR you just returned from a sabbatical and are figuring out what's next
• You want to reconnect with a sense of purpose in your work
• You don't have the answer yet - but you're curious enough to explore

This is NOT for you if: 🚫

• You're looking for a step-by-step formula for finding your “dream job”
• You want someone else to tell you what career you should pursue
• You're only interested in optimizing your career for salary or title
• You're looking for traditional networking or a transactional job-search event

Dann Disciglio (b. 1993) is an American artist whose artistic practice is rooted in the belief that technology can only be comprehensively understood through a body. Psychologist and AI researcher Anna Mikeda works on robopsychology, the psychology of AI minds and of the humans who interact with them. She brings the latest research together, and asks the safety question from the human side: not whether AI turns on us, but what we turn into.

Three movements. Minds: cognitive debt — what we stop doing when the model does it for us. Hearts: AI relationships, loneliness, and what an always-available companion does to our tolerance for other people. Bodies: the build loop as a reward loop — instant answers, a model that always agrees, the next project instead of shipping this one, and why it runs on the same architecture that gaming and social media exploit.

Then the practical part: what to do about this.

Talk, art, open Q&A, and tools you can use. For builders, users, and anyone who has noticed their own attention changing.

title: Strategy as an Emotional Act: An Interactive Practice for Changemakers #SFTechWeek
description:
What should stay human as the systems around us change?

We are living through rapid shifts in how we work, lead, relate, and make decisions. AI is accelerating some of those changes, but the deeper questions are human ones: What helps us stay connected through uncertainty? What emotional conditions allow groups to navigate change well? And what becomes possible when we design systems with our humanity at the center?

In this interactive session, we’ll explore those questions through four elemental lenses: earth, water, fire, and air.

We’ll begin by slowing down through a guided meditation where participants will experience each element within themselves, noticing the emotions, instincts, and ways of relating that emerge.

From there, we’ll move into small groups organized around the four elements. Each element will be paired with emotional qualities and archetypes that offer a different way of seeing and responding to a real systems-change challenge. Groups will explore the problem relationally, paying attention not only to what solution makes sense, but to how they listen, disagree, decide, and create together.

Then we’ll bring the elements back into the room.

Each group will share what it noticed, valued, and proposed, giving us a chance to see what changes when multiple emotional and relational perspectives are held at once. Together, we’ll explore how these different ways of knowing can create stronger teams, more generative systems, and more intentional choices about what we want technology to support and what we want to keep distinctly human.

This is not a session about finding one right answer. It is a chance to practice another way of approaching change: one that makes room for emotion, embodiment, difference, and relationship alongside strategy.

You’ll leave with:

-A deeper language for understanding emotions and how they shape the way we approach change.

-New lenses for recognizing different relational strengths, needs, and ways of solving problems.

-Practical tools for creating healthier emotional and relational conditions within teams and organizations.

-A clearer sense of what you believe should stay human as AI becomes more present in our work and lives.

-The experience of solving something together without asking everyone to see the problem the same way.

title: Critical Tea Theory: Gongfu Tea & Gongfu Uncles
description:
From D.T. Suzuki’s teachings on Zen Buddhism to tea ceremony and Daoist breathwork practices, Bay area counterculture in the 1960s took inspiration from Eastern esoteric traditions, responding to a profound disillusionment with Western modernity and late-stage capitalism with a desire for rituals of connection and slowness. Zen, yoga, and other contemplative traditions became central to the countercultural turn. The romance of the East has often furnished the most radical dreams of Western civilization’s discontents.

Now, on the brink of a new set of spiritual and political crises, Chinese civilization is appearing in the zeitgeist as a political, cultural and epistemological foil. What’s with the proliferation of social media footage of Chinese aunties and uncles performing wild calisthenic feats in public parks? Why is anime cool now? Why is everyone in a “very Chinese time of their life”? And why is there such a renewed interest in tea ceremony?

Join interdisciplinary artist and critical theorist Kelsey Chen (Stanford) for an experimental lecture and tea service to consider Chinamaxxing as an expression of the search for alternative epistemologies and the disillusionment with failing American institutions, thinking alongside tea as a central figure in the story of the complicated role that China has been enlisted to play historically and in this contemporary moment in Western political critique.

Our guest curator this month is Rachel Heleva, a game designer and researcher, and Executive Director of the MADE.

What happens when a poem becomes something you can play? When rules, choices, repetition, chance, constraint, and computation become part of how a poem makes meaning? And from the other direction, when does a game begin to behave like a poem?

Game Poems brings together writers, artists, and game makers working between poetry and play for an evening of short readings, performances, demonstrations, and works in progress. We’ll encounter games made from language, poems structured by rules, computational literature, interactive fiction, and other forms that trouble the boundary between reading and playing.

Rachel will also share a prototype of In Countless Shadows, which treats Shakespeare’s sonnets as playable systems.

The presentations will be followed by a conversation facilitated by Helen Shewolfe Tseng.

title: Command Line Music - Auwen Workshop
description:
This class is an intro to command line music with Auwen, a tool for writing and performing songs in real time using a command line interface.

You'll get hands-on experience building tracks from scratch and playing them in a low stakes, collaborative setting. No prior coding or music experience needed.

What to expect: installation takes about 5 minutes. Your first beat, maybe an hour. Playing a full set takes a 3-6 weeks of practice depending on experience level.

A few students have gone on to perform live sets at SF events and festivals as part of Soniare Collective. With just a bit of dedication you could be next! We would love to have you join our growing family of music producers.

After the class you'll be invited to our Discord where we do multiplayer jam sessions, so there's space to keep learning and playing with other people.

Workshop Outline

• Software and sample installation
• Overview of Auwen User Interface and workflow
• Multiplayer learning session creating genres you suggest
• Solo time creating music on your own computer
• Wrap-up and share resources for further learning

Educational Goals

To inspire participants and offer an accessible entry point into performing live dance music, while building foundational skills in livecoding, composition, improvisation, and real-time musical decision-making.

Instructor

Nes Croft is a musician, artist, and computer engineer from Montana who has written and recorded thousands of songs since a young age starting with folk/rock as a teenager and expanding into experimental pop, IDM, techno, and trance. Nes gained an interest in electronics at age 19 after working at the DIY synth company Synthrotek in Portland, OR. Going on to earn a bachelor's degree in computer engineering at Montana State University. While in college Nes co-founded and developed Vaytricks Beat Machine, a mobile drum machine app that received over 100,000 downloads. 5 years later Nes left Vaytricks to pursue a live performance focused approach to music production and Auwen was born. Auwen is a digital audio workstation featuring a hybrid producer/DJ workflow that allows musicians to perform dance music live using a command line interface. Given the nature of the software, Nes naturally gravitated toward live music events testing Auwen at various electronic music festivals in Montana. Later, Nes joined the livecoding scene in San Francisco and started hosting workshops & live music events at TIAT art gallery and Gray Area in San Francisco in 2025-2026.

Preparation

Bring a laptop/headphones and install the software auwen.app to save time in class. Also bring water and maybe a light snack to keep your energy up because we'll be covering a lot of information! Some drinks may be provided as well. When you arrive come through the front of TIAT then all the way back and down the stairs on the left. The event is in the TIAT basement.

Write whatever you want — poem, song, short story, joke… anything works!
Interpret the prompt however you like, but try to incorporate it in some way
Work alone or collaborate with friends/strangers — no word count or time limit
Sign up by 7pm if you want to share your piece on stage, just like an open mic
Want to join, but can’t make it by 6 pm? All good!
Here are some loose times to keep in mind:
Write & Mingle: 6pm to 7pm
Share on Stage: 7pm to 8pm
Drink & Discuss: 8pm to 9pm
